episode_summary: The team discuss a botched 2010 theft of a Stradivarius violin, how grizzly bears are used to certify bear-resistant bins and the wider world of product stress testing, Van Gogh’s reported habit of eating paint and his life, and Thomas Hardy’s macabre proposal to his second wife. It’s a whirlwind of stolen instruments, destructive testing, eccentric artists, and unconventional engagements.

facts.fact: My fact this week is that in 2010, thieves stole a strativarius worth £1.4 million, tried to sell it for £100 and couldn't find any buyers.
My fact is, there is a testing body in America which makes sure bins are bare-proof by testing them on live grizzly bears.
Okay, my fact this week is that Van Gogh, sometimes eight, has paint.
My fact this week is that the author, Thomas Hardy, proposed to his second wife by taking her to the grave of his first wife, pointing at the vacant plot near it, and saying, "That's for you."
